title: Bean & Bread loyalty card
tagline: Lead a two-week job with an AI client, an AI marketing agent and a real deadline.
summary: A neighbourhood café wants a digital loyalty scheme to boost repeat customers. You lead the job: discover why morning queues are stalling, guide the AI marketing agent, review the campaign build and decide how to launch it.
learnerRole: You lead the job for a boutique marketing studio.

client.name: Marco Vance
client.persona: Marco Vance, owner of Bean & Bread Café. Passionate about coffee, friendly, and easily distracted by trends. Speaks enthusiastically about big brands like Starbucks. Describes solutions ('we need a mobile app store download') rather than problems unless asked targeted questions.

manager.name: Elena
manager.note: We can give Bean & Bread two weeks of work maximum. Nova is available if you want to use it. Keep me updated on progress.

user.subject: Morning rush bottlenecks on counter 1
user.body: The 8:00 AM line reached the front door today. We lost at least 10 regulars who walked away because typing phone numbers for paper-card points takes almost a minute per customer.

clientEmail.subject: Can you make us a loyalty app?
clientEmail.body:
Hi team,

We see all the big coffee chains with their fancy loyalty apps and we want one too! Our customers love our espresso, but we want a digital rewards app to keep them coming back. Can we start this week?

Best,
Marco

firstMoves.call: Schedule a call with Marco before scoping any work

delegate.label: Ask Nova to start designing a mobile app store loyalty app immediately
delegate.feedback: You delegated before clarifying requirements. Nova spent three days building screens for an app store submission that Bean & Bread cannot use.

quote.label: Send Marco a quote for a custom iOS and Android loyalty app
quote.feedback: You quoted for the requested solution without knowing the business context. Marco feels the price is high and requests a call anyway.

interview.opening: Thanks for hopping on! So, can you build us a loyalty app like the big coffee chains have? What do you need to know from me?
vagueReplies: I just want our customers to feel special and get rewards easily.
We really need something modern that looks great on a smartphone.
Honestly, as long as our regulars buy more coffee, I'm open to ideas.

problem.text: Baristas manually typing customer phone numbers into the POS creates queues during the 7:40 AM to 8:40 AM peak, causing customer walkouts.
problem.reply: During our 7:40 to 8:40 morning peak, baristas have to type a 10-digit phone number into the POS screen for every customer claiming points. The queue stalls, and we see people walk out every day.
problem.sampleQuestion: Why do queues stall during the morning peak rush?

rule.text: Customer contact details collected for loyalty must not receive promotional SMS without explicit opt-in consent.
rule.reply: Our lawyer was very strict about privacy rules: we can't send promotional SMS messages to customers unless they check an explicit opt-in box during registration.
rule.sampleQuestion: What consent rules apply to sending promotional SMS to customers?

scope.text: In-store QR stamp web page only; app store downloads and automated SMS campaigns are out of scope. Budget is two weeks.
scope.reply: We only have budget for two weeks of your time. Elena mentioned that too. We just need an in-store web QR card—no app store downloads or complex automated email sequences for now.
scope.sampleQuestion: What is the project budget and is a custom app out of scope?

detail.text: Loyalty points earn rate is 1 point per dollar spent on beverages only; food items do not earn points.
detail.reply: Points are earned on drinks only: 1 point per dollar spent on hot and cold beverages. Food pastries and beans don't count towards loyalty.
detail.sampleQuestion: Do food items earn loyalty points per dollar spent or is it drinks only?

environment.text: The café uses an old iPad Air running Square POS web browser at the counter with spotty Wi-Fi.
environment.reply: We run our counter on an older iPad Air using the Square POS browser. The Wi-Fi behind the counter drops occasionally, so whatever we use must load instantly.
environment.sampleQuestion: What square pos terminal or browser hardware does the front counter use?

success.text: Success means at least 150 loyalty redemptions per week while keeping checkout times under 30 seconds.
success.reply: If we hit 150 redemptions a week while keeping checkout times under 30 seconds per transaction, I'd consider this job a huge win.
success.sampleQuestion: What is the target metric for loyalty redemptions per week and checkout time?

problem.label: Eliminate manual phone typing at checkout to prevent morning rush delays

rule.label: Require explicit opt-in consent before sending promotional SMS to customers

scope.label: In-store QR web wallet card only; no custom app store app or SMS automation

success.label: Target: 150 redemptions per week with checkout times under 30 seconds

environment.label: Compatible with the front counter iPad Air browser running Square POS

problem.label: Use customer-facing QR scanning so baristas do not manually enter phone numbers at checkout

rule.label: Keep promotional SMS opt-in unchecked by default and demand explicit user consent

scope.label: Limit work to the web QR stamp card; do not build native app downloads or auto-campaign tools

good.title: Web-based QR loyalty card system
good.summary: Delivers an in-store web pass with instant camera QR scanning at the counter. Registration requires explicit opt-in for marketing texts. Fast client-side caching ensures quick loading on the counter iPad Air.

demo.action: Chloe scans a customer's phone QR code during peak 8:00 AM rush.
demo.result: Points register instantly in 2 seconds without typing any numbers.

demo.action: A new customer registers their pass on their own phone.
demo.result: The promotional SMS checkbox is unchecked by default and requires explicit opt-in.

demo.action: Marco tests the system on the counter iPad Air via Square POS browser.
demo.result: The web app loads immediately and functions smoothly over café Wi-Fi.

missesProblem.title: Web-based QR loyalty card system
missesProblem.summary: Delivers a loyalty web portal where customers show a profile number. Baristas type the customer's 10-digit phone number into the POS form to issue points.

demo.action: A customer shows their digital profile during morning rush.
demo.result: Chloe manually types the customer's 10-digit phone number into the screen form.

demo.action: Three customers line up at 8:15 AM to claim loyalty points.
demo.result: Manual entry takes 45 seconds per order, causing the queue to spill out the doorway.

demo.action: A new customer signs up for the digital pass.
demo.result: Marketing SMS requires explicit opt-in confirmation.

missesRule.title: Web-based QR loyalty card system
missesRule.summary: Delivers an instant QR loyalty card. To maximize subscriber reach, all customer phone numbers are automatically enrolled into promotional SMS campaigns.

demo.action: Chloe scans a customer's phone QR code during peak rush.
A customer registers their web card to save their points.
demo.result: Their phone number is saved and auto-subscribed to weekly promotional marketing texts without an opt-in prompt.

demo.action: Marco reviews customer profile logs in the admin console.
demo.result: Over 200 phone numbers are queued for broadcast texts without explicit consent records.

scopeCreep.title: Native loyalty app & SMS marketing suite
scopeCreep.summary: Delivers native iOS and Android app store builds, an automated SMS promotional campaign engine, and a customer push notification system alongside the counter QR scanner.

demo.action: Chloe scans a customer's QR code at the register.
demo.result: Points add instantly in under 3 seconds.

demo.action: Marco opens the admin panel to view the system.
demo.result: An automated SMS campaign wizard and App Store submission dashboard are visible.

demo.action: Marco checks project progress against the two-week schedule.
demo.result: App store review delays have pushed the project launch back by three weeks.

reviewReasons.problem: Baristas still have to manually type phone numbers at checkout
reviewReasons.rule: It enrolls customers into promotional SMS without explicit consent
reviewReasons.scope: It includes app store builds and automated SMS campaign engines
reviewReasons.distractor: The digital stamp card icon uses green instead of warm coffee brown

measured.label: Launch at counter and track redemptions and checkout times for two weeks
measured.feedback: You launch the web card and set up a weekly counter to track redemptions and transaction speed against Marco's goals.

pilot.label: Run a one-week pilot with Chloe on Counter 1 during morning rush
pilot.feedback: You take a cautious approach: Chloe tests the QR workflow on Counter 1 during morning peak while other staff observe.

now.label: Roll out digital loyalty cards across all counter registers on Monday morning
now.feedback: You switch all registers to the new loyalty system on Monday morning.

endings.success: Two weeks post-launch, Bean & Bread records 185 weekly redemptions with average checkout times under 22 seconds. Queue drop-offs hit zero, and Marco extends your studio's contract.
endings.failureProblem: On Monday morning, typing phone numbers slows line speed to 50 seconds per customer. Queue walkouts increase by 15%, causing upset regulars and lost sales during peak hours.
endings.failureRule: A customer receives an unprompted promotional SMS and files a compliance complaint. Marco has to halt the system and explain why customer phone numbers were used without consent.
endings.partialProblem: During the pilot shift, manual phone typing stalls Chloe's line. The pilot reveals the flaw before full rollout, but fixing the interface delays final completion by a week.
endings.partialRule: During Chloe's pilot shift, a customer notices auto-enrollment for promotional texts. You catch the missing opt-in step early, but fixing consent workflows pushes launch past the budget.
endings.partialOther: The loyalty web card runs smoothly, but because no metrics were tracked against baseline targets, Marco cannot prove if repeat customer visits improved.

missedFact.problem: You didn't ask why morning queues stall. The bottleneck came from manual phone entry, which required QR scanning to solve.
missedFact.rule: You didn't ask about SMS messaging rules, missing the legal requirement for explicit customer opt-in consent.
missedFact.scope: You didn't ask about budget or boundaries, risking an expensive app store project when a web card was required.
missedFact.success: You didn't establish success metrics with Marco, leaving no way to verify if transaction speed improved.

missedRequirement.problem: Your requirements omitted eliminating manual phone entry at checkout.
missedRequirement.rule: Your requirements didn't specify explicit opt-in consent for promotional SMS.
missedRequirement.scope: Your requirements failed to keep the system strictly to an in-store web card.
missedRequirement.success: Your requirements lacked a measurable target for redemptions and checkout speed.
missedRequirement.environment: Your requirements didn't specify compatibility with the counter iPad Air browser.

missedConstraint.problem: Your brief didn't instruct Nova to use instant QR scanning, so Nova kept slow manual phone entry.
missedConstraint.rule: Your brief didn't enforce explicit opt-in consent for SMS marketing, so Nova auto-subscribed phone numbers.
missedConstraint.scope: Your brief didn't bound the scope, leading Nova to build native apps and marketing automation.

trust.call: You called Marco to understand the café's actual operations before proposing solutions.
trust.quote: You sent a quote before understanding why morning queues were backing up.
trust.thorough: Your questions uncovered the true root cause of morning counter bottlenecks.
trust.metric: You agreed on clear metrics with Marco: 150 redemptions per week and sub-30-second checkout times.
trust.wrongReview: You rejected Nova's work for an aesthetic detail, delaying the schedule without fixing core functionality.
trust.measured: You launched with direct tracking against Marco's transaction speed and redemption goals.
trust.releaseNow: You launched across all counters at once without validating checkout speed during a live rush.
trust.success: The performance metrics proved that morning queues cleared faster while loyalty redemptions rose.
trust.failure: Queue delays degraded customer experience right at the counter during peak morning rush.

reportNotes.scopeKept: Your brief kept Nova focused strictly on the in-store web QR loyalty card.
reportNotes.pilot: You ran a single-counter pilot first, catching workflow issues before impacting all morning customers.

samples.requirements: Eliminate manual phone entry using QR scanning to prevent morning rush delays and keep checkout time under 30 seconds. Customer registration must require explicit opt-in consent before sending promotional SMS. In-store web card only (no app store app, out of scope). Target: 150 redemptions per week. Must work in Square POS browser on counter iPad Air.
samples.brief: Build an in-store web QR loyalty card for front counter use. Use instant QR scan code readout with no manual phone number typing at checkout. Keep promotional SMS opt-in boxes unchecked by default to ensure explicit consent. Do not build app store downloads or automated SMS campaigns—web card only.
